Doctor Blade Coatings: Quality Check Using Microscopy Coatings of the AFL, ASL and GDC slurries were cast using the doctor blade method onto Mylar. The coatings were dried in a ventilated enclosure within a dry room, at room temperature. Each dry film’s thickness was measured and a Keyence VHX-1000 microscope was used to evaluate differences in morphology between slurries with varying concentrations of solid loading. It was noted that after drying, surface defects such as air entrapment and cracks became visible in certain samples. Features such as grain structure, surface roughness, and surface defects were observed under varying magnifications and using software assisted 3D surface analysis. After drying, certain defects can be reduced by calendering to fill in gaps and cracks with binder, or formulation changes can be made to increase polymeric binders that increase contact between the active materials. Figures 14-17 show the image of the various coatings. For the ASL coating, lower solid content could result in cracks when forming thick films. The AFL and GDC coatings seem similar.
